title: why small interfaces matter
excerpt: a short talk on tiny surfaces — why the first honest frame beats a dashboard full of undecided features.

blocks.text: a short talk on tiny surfaces — why the first honest frame beats a dashboard full of undecided features.

this piece starts from a small observation and widens only when the frame still holds. why small interfaces matter is less a finished argument than a working note: what changes if we treat the interface as a place to practice judgment, not just to display outputs.

the method is deliberate. read the constraint first — time, width, material — then let the form follow. when the draft runs ahead of the hand, pull it back. when the hand freezes, let the draft move a few steps and see what becomes legible.

if there is an image nearby, treat it as furniture in the argument: something you walk around, not a caption you ignore. the point is not polish; it is a surface honest enough that someone else can hold it.
